The project formalized $
um{10657}$ positive implications and $
um{586925}$ negative implications, with the latter in turn organized into $
um{1322}$ 	exttt{Facts} theorems as discussed above.  Explicitly formalizing all $
um{22028942}$ implications as theorems would lead to an infeasible compilation time in \emph{Lean}; formalizing all positive implications alone would increase the number of theorems by a factor of $800$.  Instead, a reduced generating set that was sufficient to decide the entire implication graph was formalized.  The extension of these results to the rest of the implication graph via transitivity and duality is carried out within \emph{Lean} by an ``end-to-end theorem'', 	exttt{end\_to\_end1}, which uses a pre-processed certificate to show that every ordered pair of laws has either a derivation from the proven implications or a refutation by one of the project's model witnesses.  This theorem concerns general magmas; for the finite implication graph, the corresponding extension is still done by programs external to \emph{Lean}.
